lacuna.name: campaign-provenance-intent
lacuna.repo_anchor: The host's own doctrine states the acceptance test this item researches: AGENTS.md - 'a new session with no memory of this conversation should be able to read plan/, call/, and MEMORY.md and continue without repeating a past mistake'. call/0005 (2026-09-08, integrate-research-into-plans) already legislates the integration pass: findings mapped onto plan READMEs, 'corrections written back into the records they invalidate (a MEMORY-only correction is insufficient)', research/CONSOLIDATION.md maintained as the front door (material map, final-truth topics, retraction ledger, uncertainty register), and 'counts and numerical claims in the run's own summary verified by script before commit (the 49/120 lesson)' - the recorded incident where a summary asserted 49 uncertainty markers against 120 verified. MEMORY.md is the append-only contemporaneous session log (one entry per window/phase, e.g. '2026-09-11 (72h window CLOSED at ~11h of 72, all plan phases delivered)' carrying the final ledger plus the next-window queue; corrections are new entries pointing back: '2026-09-08 (CORRECTION): the earlier kmap findings ... are INVALID ... the probe's host D buffer was 16 floats against 64 written'). The champion verdict record exists in two forms: vllm_ab_run.py writes ab-ledger.json entries and renders ab-champion-ledger.md ('## 2026-09-10T03:51:58 - bridge-gather vs bridge-paged (... graphs=on)' with per-row '- ctx512_decode: 25.9 vs 12.9 (-50.2 pct, gate 76.0 pct) -> NO_DIFF'; verdict() computes medians, a spread-derived gate max(5.0, 300.0*sigma), A_WINS/B_WINS/NO_DIFF), and prose entries carry intent by hand ('DISPOSITION: MTP serves on the gather path (proven); the combination stays disabled; root-cause owned by Phase D'). NEXT-WINDOW-RUNBOOK.md is the resume-intent document - turnkey ordered sequence with deciding rows, refreshed per window, with a 'Superseded history ... Kept for provenance' section. The provenance failure already paid for is recorded in MEMORY 2026-09-08: 'a half-done revert sat staged in the vendored flash-attn tree ... AND the lane's kld-split/d256 kernel API lived only as uncommitted edits the whole engine path depends on'; the remedy was commit-plus-archive ('the load-bearing kernel edits are NOW COMMITTED (lane f4b708b122) ... rebuild = upstream v2.8.3 + git am in order'). The gap this item researches is on the runner side: the weco local loop's steps.jsonl records state only ({step, value, improved_best, output_tail}) - no hypothesis, no why, no disposition - so an interrupted or cold-read session can reconstruct WHAT happened but not WHAT THE RUN WAS TRYING TO DO.
lacuna.current_status: As of 2026-09 every surveyed domain answers the same question - what must a record carry so a reader with no shared context can resume intent - and the answers converge. (1) Reproducible-research provenance: the founding claim is Claerbout's motto as reproduced in Buckheit & Donoho, 'Wavelab and Reproducible Research' (Stanford TR, 1995): 'An article about computational science in a scientific publication is not the scholarship itself, it is merely an advertisement of the scholarship. The actual scholarship is the complete software development environment and the complete set of instructions which generated the figures.' Claerbout's Stanford Exploration Project ladder grades a publication by what ships with it: text+figures, then the software, then the data, then per-figure regeneration scripts, then a full buildable tree [uncertain: exact level numbering - SEP primary unreachable this run; quote verified via Stodden's 'Reproducibility in Computational Science' and the National Academies 'Fostering Integrity in Research' reproduction]. Victoria Stodden's Reproducible Research Standard (~2010) and 'Setting the Default to Reproducible' (ICERM workshop report 2012; SIAM News 2013) propose releasing the four components of computational scholarship - data, methods/code, workflow and documentation, and the paper - under permissive licenses. Stodden, Miguez & Seiler, 'Best Practices for Computational Science' (Journal of Open Research Software, 2014) carries the operative rule: 'Workflow tracking should be carried out during the research process' - version control plus an issue tracker, planning board, or open notebook recording provenance AS the work happens, not at write-up; data get versions, hashes, and access timestamps; environments are recorded beside the code. The ML analog of a minimal paper-facing schema is the Pineau et al. machine-learning reproducibility checklist (introduced at NeurIPS 2018; 'Improving Reproducibility in Machine Learning Research', JMLR 2021): a fixed question list (baselines, hyperparameters, seeds, compute, code availability) the author answers per paper. (2) Experiment trackers: MLflow's run record (params, metrics, tags, artifacts under an experiment) is enriched by auto-captured system tags - verified in source (mlflow/utils/mlflow_tags.py, tracking/context/git_context.py, master 2026-09-11): mlflow.user, mlflow.source.name/type, mlflow.source.git.commit/branch/repoURL, mlflow.source.git.dirty AND mlflow.source.git.diff (the uncommitted diff folded into the run record), mlflow.runName, mlflow.note.content (the free-text run description), mlflow.parentRunId (parent-child lineage). Weights & Biases: every run carries config, summary, and notes, where notes is documented as 'A detailed description of the run, similar to a commit message in Git' (init() reference) - intent is explicitly the commit-message analog; sweeps are first-class campaign objects with pause/resume state; artifacts version datasets/models with lineage; known defect: successive wandb.init() calls during sweeps can overwrite notes (wandb#5119). ClearML auto-captures the repo URL, commit ID, AND uncommitted diff per task and warns when running uncommitted code (docs FAQ + task SDK); caveat: staged-but-uncommitted changes escape the captured diff (clearml#457). Cross-tracker finding: state is captured mechanically and richly; intent lives in exactly one optional free-text field (notes) - the thinnest slot in every tool, and the one a campaign actually resumes from. (3) Electronic lab notebooks: ELNs record 'protocols, observations, notes, and other data' with 'automatic date and time stamping to prove provenance and improve record-keeping' (Harvard Biomedical Data Management guide); UKRN frames ELNs as 'accurate documentation of research processes' with immediate data+metadata capture serving FAIR; the regulatory floor is ALCOA+ under FDA 21 CFR Part 11 / MHRA GxP data-integrity guidance: records Attributable, Legible, Contemporaneous (written at the time of the activity, never backfilled), Original, Accurate, plus Complete/Consistent/Enduring/Available, with append-only audit trails [uncertain: MHRA edition not fetched]; practice guidance adds: plan the entry structure (naming, tags) before the campaign, link every entry to its data, enter timely/consistent entries, keep records retrievable when personnel leave. (4) Post-incident records: the US Army After Action Review (1970s; Garvin's HBR treatment) is four fixed questions - 'What did we set out to do? What actually happened? Why did it happen? What are we going to do about it?' - forward-looking, beginning from 'a clear comparison of intended versus actual results', inside a cycle that starts by 'establishing the leader's intent'; commander's intent doctrine (US JP 3-0) defines the resume artifact itself - 'a clear and concise expression of the purpose of the operation and the military end state', short enough to be understood two echelons down, existing precisely so subordinates act correctly when orders no longer fit the situation. Blameless postmortem practice (Etsy/Allspaw 2012; Google SRE Workbook ch. 10) fixes the format: quantified impact, root cause and trigger, timeline, lessons (what went well/poorly/lucky), and action items each with ONE owner, a priority, a tracking bug, and a measurable end state; 'to our users, a postmortem without subsequent action is indistinguishable from no postmortem'; the audience 'extends beyond the immediate team', so reports carry Background and Glossary sections and abstract long logs into appendices. (5) Commit messages and decision records: Chris Beams' canonical rules (cbea.ms) - subject plus body, and the body explains what and WHY: 'A diff will tell you what changed, but only the commit message can properly tell you why'; 'the future maintainer that thanks you may be yourself'. Nygard's ADRs (2011) - numbered one-to-two-page records with Title/Context/Decision/Status/Consequences, superseded in place rather than deleted, written 'as if it is a conversation with a future developer', with 'the consequences of one ADR ... very likely to become the context for subsequent ADRs', and the upkeep warning that large documents are never kept current while small modular ones are. (6) Agent-session handoff (2025-2026, fast-moving): Anthropic's multi-agent research system post requires every delegated task to carry 'an objective, an output format, guidance on the tools and sources to use, and clear task boundaries'; the LeadResearcher starts by 'saving its plan to Memory to persist the context' ahead of 200k-token truncation; agents 'spawn fresh subagents with clean contexts while maintaining continuity through careful handoffs' and 'store their work in external systems, then pass lightweight references back to the coordinator', explicitly avoiding a 'game of telephone'. Cognition's 'Don't Build Multi-Agents' (2025) states 'share the full context, and share full agent traces, not just individual messages' because 'actions carry implicit decisions' that a summary strips; when compression is unavoidable it compresses 'a history of actions & conversation into key details, events, and decisions' - a three-field resume-intent record by name. Manus' context-engineering post makes 'the file system ... the ultimate context: unlimited in size, persistent by nature, and directly operable', keeps a todo.md as 'a deliberate mechanism to manipulate attention' ('reciting its objectives into the end of the context') against goal drift over ~50-tool-call tasks, and demands reversible compression (drop content, keep the URL/path). AGENTS.md (60k+ projects, stewarded by the Agentic AI Foundation under the Linux Foundation; contributors include OpenAI Codex, Cursor, Amp, Jules) is the checked-in 'README for agents' - 'anything you'd tell a new teammate', nested with nearest-file-wins scoping. OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions (repo open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai, all Development status 2026-09) define spans for create_agent/invoke_agent/execute_tool and a plan span ('agent planning or task decomposition phase'), with gen_ai.conversation.id correlating a session's records - the emerging machine-readable session-provenance wire format. Karpathy's autoresearch (2026) closes the loop for overnight agents: intent lives in program.md, the file the HUMAN edits and versions while the agent only reads it; the morning deliverable is 'a log of experiments' the human reviews.
lacuna.applicability: Transfers to the weco-local long-range runner: (1) The host already runs the target pattern at window cadence, by hand - MEMORY.md is the contemporaneous append-only lab notebook (ALCOA's attributable/contemporaneous/original, already enforced by the append-only rule), the champion ledger is the per-verdict record with evidence and a spread-derived gate, the runbook is the commander's-intent-plus-ordered-queue resume document, and call/0005's integration pass is the corrections-write-back discipline; what transfers from the research is making these MECHANICAL and schema'd rather than heroic. (2) Per-verdict intent fields: the ledger's JSON entries already capture arms/rows/gate/verdict (state); the four fields every surveyed domain adds are question (the hypothesis under test - the ADR Context / W&B notes / commit-message-body slot), mechanism (why the verdict came out as it did), disposition/next (the single next action with its deciding row - the SRE action item with measurable end state), and provenance (lane sha + dirty flag + diff captured AT verdict time - the ClearML/MLflow lesson that provenance is captured in-line, never reconstructed from memory; this host already paid the flash-attn price for the missing version). (3) Per-day window record generated at close: the AAR four questions plus a two-sentence commander's-intent header, verdicts included as lightweight ledger pointers (Anthropic's telephone-game defense), corrections as entries naming the record corrected (call/0005 write-back), script-verified counts (the 49/120 lesson), and the next_queue with gates and deciding rows that becomes the runbook's next GPU queue verbatim. (4) The weco steps.jsonl gains a one-line hypothesis per step - without it the loop's own log is state-only (value, improved_best, output_tail) and a resumed session optimizes blind; the commit-message-body analogy is exact (the diff tells what, the field tells why). (5) Resume protocol: a fixed read order (MEMORY tail -> runbook -> ledger tail -> latest day record) as the runbook's opening section, so the cold-start path is itself recorded. Does NOT transfer: MLflow/W&B/ClearML as tools - this host's records are committed files in sanctioned rooms, and a tracker database is foreign state the gates cannot read (only their schema lessons transfer); the ELN regulatory apparatus (witness countersignature, 21 CFR Part 11 e-signatures, audit-trail software) - a single-operator research campaign has no regulatory chain of custody, only the contemporaneous/append-only core matters and the host already has it; OTel GenAI telemetry - a single-host two-GPU loop does not need a distributed wire standard (the conversation.id correlation idea is already realized by ledger timestamps); Stodden's publication-side obligations (permissive licensing of all four components, external perpetual deposit) - addressed to releasing scholarship, not campaign continuity, though its data-hash-and-version rule is the same discipline as the host's .host-software pins; Sacred-class frameworks - superseded for this purpose by the ledger the host already owns.

design.mechanism: The minimal record schema a 72h campaign writes, implementable cold. (A) PER-VERDICT RECORD - extend each ab-ledger.json entry written by vllm_ab_run.py with four fields (mechanical fields already exist): {ts, question, arm_a:{label,config}, arm_b:{label,config}, rows:{metric:{a_median,b_median,delta_pct,gate_pct,verdict}}, provenance:{lane_sha, dirty, diff_ref, preflight_ok}, mechanism, disposition:{use: keep|refute|withheld, next, deciding_row}}. question: one sentence naming the hypothesis under test ('does chunking the page walk fix the ctx2048 collapse'). mechanism: why the verdict is what it is, or the explicit value 'unknown - bisect queued' (a NO_DIFF with a named mechanism or a named discriminating follow-up, never a bare number). disposition.next: the single next action a cold session takes; deciding_row: the metric row that decides it. provenance: captured IN the harness at verdict time - git rev-parse HEAD, --porcelain for dirty, and when dirty the diff written to results/provenance/<ts>.diff (ClearML/MLflow dirty-diff analog; the flash-attn lesson made mechanical). (B) PER-DAY WINDOW RECORD - one generated markdown per day (results/<campaign>/days/YYYY-MM-DD.md), produced by the campaign-runner close step and committed BEFORE clocks are restored; eleven fields: (1) header {window, date, author, open/close, preflight verdict}; (2) intent - the campaign goal plus today's end state, two sentences maximum (commander's intent: purpose + end state, JP 3-0); (3) plan - the ordered queue exactly as the day opened (AAR question 1; the runbook's GPU queue verbatim); (4) verdicts - ledger pointers only, no re-narrated numbers (lightweight references; the telephone-game defense); (5) deltas - intended-vs-actual divergences and why (AAR questions 2-3); (6) corrections - retracted claims, each naming the record it corrects (MEMORY correction pattern; call/0005 write-back; never in-place rewrite); (7) counts - the record's own numerical claims verified by script before commit (the 49/120 rule); (8) open_questions - ranked, each with the experiment that would close it; (9) next_queue - ordered, each item = action + gate + deciding row (AAR question 4; the Manus todo.md forward plan), becoming the runbook's next GPU queue verbatim; (10) provenance - lane shas touched, environment pins, artifact paths (Stodden rule 2); (11) resume - the cold-start read order: MEMORY tail -> runbook -> ledger tail -> this record (the AGENTS.md entry-point pattern). (C) RESUME PROTOCOL (doctrine): a cold session executes the resume list, then next_queue, with no chat log; the acceptance test is the host's own sentence - a new session continues without repeating a past mistake. (D) WECO steps.jsonl: add one field per step {hypothesis: '<one line: what this mutation believes it improves and why>'} - the commit-message-body slot for the loop's own append-only log; resume reads the trailing hypotheses to reconstruct search direction (the Manus recitation against drift).
design.failure_modes: Documented failure modes and defenses: (1) Intent dies with the context window - summaries strip the implicit decisions actions carry, and relayed paraphrases play 'a game of telephone' (Cognition; Anthropic); defense: file-based records with lightweight pointers to raw artifacts, never re-narrated numbers. (2) Backfilled entries rewrite history - the ALCOA contemporaneous principle exists because retrospective reconstruction is untrustworthy; in-place mutable notes also get clobbered (wandb#5119 sweep runs overwriting notes); defense: generated-at-close timestamps, append-only ledgers, corrections as new entries pointing back (the MEMORY pattern already in force). (3) The unresumable number - a verdict recorded without its mechanism cannot be acted on by a cold reader (every postmortem template demands root cause); defense: mechanism mandatory, 'unknown - bisect queued' legal, disposition.next required. (4) Provenance reconstructed from memory - ClearML captures the diff at task creation and MLflow at run start precisely because after-the-fact reconstruction is wrong or impossible; this host's instance was load-bearing kernel API living only as uncommitted edits for a whole window; defense: sha+dirty+diff captured in the harness at verdict time, tree committed before the window closes. (5) Fabricated summary precision - the host's own 49-asserted-vs-120-verified incident, invisible to every gate that does not read research output; defense: script-verified counts (call/0005 rule 4) and pointers over re-narration. (6) Record bloat kills upkeep - large documents 'are never kept current' (Nygard); defense: minimal fields, records GENERATED from the ledger and git, one home per fact (the host's pointer-over-restatement rule). (7) The postmortem that changes nothing - 'indistinguishable from no postmortem' (SRE); defense: next_queue items each carry gate, deciding row, and owner. (8) Goal drift over long horizons - todo.md exists because ~50 tool calls lose the plan (Manus); a 72h campaign is thousands of steps; defense: intent recited in every day-record header and every step hypothesis. (9) Silent supersession - a reversed verdict whose old entry disappears loses the lesson; defense: retracted entries kept and marked with a pointer to the correcting entry (ADR superseded-status; CONSOLIDATION retraction ledger). (10) Records nobody finds - the audience 'extends beyond the immediate team' (SRE) and agents bootstrap from checked-in files (AGENTS.md); defense: the resume field IS part of the schema, day records sit beside the runbook in the committed tree, never in chat.
design.effort_estimate: Wrapper-level plus two small fork-level patches. vllm_ab_run.py (lane-local): +4 entry fields and the in-harness provenance capture (~30 lines). tools/campaign-runner close-out (new, stdlib only): day-record generator reading ab-ledger.json + git state + preflight log, MEMORY.md append, runbook next-queue rewrite (~80 lines shell/python). weco-cli fork (precedent: connollydavid/weco-cli#1): steps.jsonl hypothesis field (~10 lines). Doctrine-only: the resume protocol and day-record cadence written into the runbook's open/close sequence. No new services, no MLflow/W&B/ClearML dependency.
design.priority_signal: For: the 72h window's continuity lived entirely in hand-written MEMORY entries and a manually refreshed runbook - it worked because the writing session was the same session that ran the campaign, which is precisely the condition a cold resume or a multi-day unattended run removes; the flash-attn near-loss (load-bearing edits uncommitted for a whole window) is the provenance failure mode already realized once on this host; the schema is ~80 percent built (ledger + MEMORY + runbook + CONSOLIDATION all exist and are committed), every added field maps to a decades-old precedent (AAR four questions, commander's intent, ALCOA contemporaneous, ADR context/consequences, commit-message body, SRE action items), and the cost is a few dozen lines plus a generation step. Against: this is discipline-automation, not a capability gap - supervision (timeouts, watchdog) and checkpoint/resume must land first, because a dead campaign writes no records and a loop that restarts at step 0 has no accumulated intent worth resuming; there is a real risk the schema accretes until record-keeping crowds out research (Nygard's upkeep warning), so it must stay at the minimal fields and be generated, never hand-authored; and the single-operator reality means the attribution/witness machinery of regulated ELNs buys nothing here. Net: land the per-verdict fields and the generated day record as the close-out step of the same campaign-runner change that lands supervision and resume - one coherent close ritual, not a separate effort.
